core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 1052-1056): the author sets u = (g, f) : w -> x plus y and v = (k, -h) : x plus y -> z, lets p and q be the canonical projections and i the canonical injection of the kernel of v.

Part (1) (proof lines 1056-1065): by the cited example the square is cartesian exactly when there is an isomorphism r from the kernel of v to w with f r = q i and g r = p i, while the displayed three-term sequence is exact exactly when there is an isomorphism r with u r = i; the two conditions on r are equivalent because the components of u are g and f, so the two isomorphisms coincide.
Part (2) (proof line 1065): the cocartesian statement follows from the cartesian one by duality.
proof_roadmap: Write the pair of maps through the direct sum and the canonical projections.
Compare the description of the fibre product with exactness of the three-term sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma translates cartesianness and cocartesianness of a commutative square in an abelian category into exactness of a sequence built from the direct sum of the two inner objects (statement lines 1025-1049). The proof is a complete argument: the fibre product is identified with the kernel of the map out of the direct sum by a named example, and both the cartesian condition and the exactness condition are then expressed as the existence of an isomorphism out of that kernel with the same two components, which is where the equivalence is read off (proof lines 1052-1065); the cocartesian statement is obtained by duality. The non-formal content is the translation between the two descriptions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
